newsitem.title: CANADA: Former Confederation Life properties to be sold.
newsitem.headline: Former Confederation Life properties to be sold.

text.p: Twelve properties formerly owned by the now bankrupt Confederation Life Insurance Co are being put on sale to take advantage of the recent resurgence of the Canadian real estate market.

Accounting and consulting firm KMPG said on Monday it would soon be accepting bids on the properties. KMPG will act as an agent for the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, a federal regulator serving as the provisional liquidator of Confederation Life.
The federal regulator said it hoped to sell the portfolio as a package but would accept bids on single properties or parts of the porfolio.

"While our initial intention was to dispose of these assets over a seven to 10-year period, continued improvement in the real estate markets has caused us to reassess our strategy," KPMG Inc President Bob Sanderson said in a statement.

The portfolio includes interests in seven office properties with about 3.2 million square feet of leasable space, and five retail properties with about 2.4 million square feet of leasable space. Five of the properties are co-owned with other investors.
The sale of the Conferation properties is the second major portfolio to hit the market this summer.

Prudential Insurance Co of America last week agreed to sell its Canadian real estate portfolio to a 50/50 joint venture of Oxford Properties Group Inc and GE Capital Canada Inc for about C$455.8 million. The 48 properties in that portfolio included five Toronto land parcels and 43 commercial properties across Canada comprising about 5.6 million square feet of rentable space.

"It's clearly reflective of the recovery under way in the real estate markets, and also the activity and strength of the capital markets with respect to real estate stocks in general, which has allowed a lot of these companies to raise funds to acquire properties," Mike Hough, a real estate analyst with HSBC James Capel Canada, told Reuters.
Oxford Properties and TrizecHahn Corp, which also bid on the Prudential portfolio, were likely candidates to bid on all or part of the Confederation properties, Hough said.
The properties being sold are in Toronto, Calgary, Edmonton, Vancouver and Winnipeg.

The properties being offered, which are wholly owned include: Airway Centre, 2200 Lakeshore Boulevard West/10 Parklawn Road and Hazelton Lanes in the Toronto area, the Lime Ridge Mall Land Lease in Hamilton, 736-6th Avenue S.W. in Calgary and Capilano Mall and Edmonton Eaton Centre Complex.
The co-owned properties being sold are Parkway Place and Dixie Outlet Mall in Toronto, 400 St. Mary Avenue in Winnipeg, Canterra Tower in Calgary and Metropolitan Place in Edmonton.
KMPG said the sale would be conducted through a competitive process in three phases, including the creation of a short-list of bidders, and should be completed before the end of the year.
